page.layout: One page of text, no margin notes. Top: decorative ornament (not transcribed). Below it, centred: the author's name and title line, then the heading "PRÆFATIO AD LECTOREM.", then one paragraph of running text opening with a large woodcut initial. No page number, running head, catchword or signature.

main_text.head: PETRI MATTHÆI I. C. Lugdun.
PRÆFATIO AD LECTOREM.
main_text.p: ISAACVS CA-SAVBONVS, cui nec desunt vires, nec languent animi, ad studiorum fulcien-das ruinas, Lugdunum venit, eo maxime tempore, quo tota ciuitas ob sal. publ. & restitutam pacem, post tot malorum maria e sagis ad togas re-dierat, & ingenti laetitia apparatu defudabat. Diuertit ad amplissi-mum D. de Vic, Regis ab in-timis consiliis, Tholosani Senatus Præsi

page.notes: The large initial is a woodcut; I read it as "I" with the first word continuing in small capitals ("ISAACVS"). The printed text has "Saacus" in small capitals with "I" as the initial. The paragraph ends mid-word at "Præsi" and continues on the next page. Ornament at top not transcribed.
